goal: Users can select a school template, understand and filter stable zh-CN structured diagnostics, activate source-linked issues, and build only when no error-severity diagnostic remains.
non_goals: Do not change template schema, resolver precedence, validator rules, compiler, renderer, numbering, bibliography, or DOCX behavior.
Do not implement arbitrary browser-native template paths, final packaged template discovery, outline/preview mapping, streamed progress, cancellation, or release acceptance.
Do not introduce direct React-to-HTTP/Tauri/Python calls, autosave, database, accounts, AI, telemetry, dark mode, or runtime locale switching.
expected_evidence: Strict TDD RED and GREEN for Python/TypeScript zh-CN diagnostic mapping parity and unknown-code fallback
Reducer and selector tests for template state, deterministic ordering, filtering, counts, active issue, fatal guard, and warning-only build
Component tests for template-triggered revalidation, diagnostic rows, keyboard/pointer activation, editor line focus, and no-line issues
Transport and adapter tests proving stable templateId resolution, templatePath compatibility, selector-conflict rejection, and complete diagnostic DTO validation
Real validation-service tests for valid, missing, malformed, and incompatible templates
Frontend unit/typecheck/lint/build/E2E and focused/full Python regression evidence
Ruff, pip check, strict OpenSpec, SpecNav entry, CodeGraph, JSON, and whitespace evidence
Task report, dedicated spec review, and dedicated quality review
unsafe_assumptions: Template selector presence proves resolver integration.
Every diagnostic has a line or a known localization code.
Frontend filtering may discard diagnostics or mutate Markdown.
A shallow successful transport response proves diagnostic DTO validity.
The frontend fatal guard can replace the application build validation gate.
stop_condition: Stop if implementation needs resolver/template-schema semantics changes, edits outside allowed files, direct frontend runtime or compiler coupling, arbitrary Web filesystem disclosure, dropped diagnostic fields, duplicated localization/filter/navigation logic, or any weakening of application-layer fatal validation.
